**Cameroon General Certificate of Education Board - Advanced Level Examination. Information & Communication Technologies, Subject code 0796, Paper 3 (practical). Examination date: June 2021. Duration: two hours. The paper was set in two versions in the same document: Day 1 (booklet GCE/P/2021/0796/3/C/G1, workbook Trans-Business) and Day 2 (booklet GCE/P/2021/0796/3/C/G2, workbook Car Sales). Enter the information required in the shaded boxes. Do not write in pencil. You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answer. **DAY 2**

**TASK A: DATABASES (21 marks)**

A car dealer has 10 brokers (middle men who look for buyers) in his car shops in the towns of Douala, Kumba, Buea and Bamenda.

Part of the information about the sales of his cars is found in a workbook named **Car Sales** found in the *Candidate Folder*. This workbook contains two sheets named **Broker** and **Sales**. The personal information of the brokers is stored in the sheet named **Broker** while the transaction carried out by the brokers is recorded in the sheet named **Sales**.

The table below shows the description of the cars found in the car shops in the four towns.

*Table 1: Cars*

| CarCode | CarName | UnitPrice |
|---|---|---|
| AB1 | Toyota Avensis | 2500000 |
| CD2 | Toyota Corolla | 2300000 |
| M41 | BMW Picnic | 2625000 |
| AB2 | Mercedes 220 | 1800000 |
| NS3 | Mercedes 300 | 3000000 |

*[The workbook Car Sales (sheets Broker and Sales) is supplied on the day in the candidate folder; it is not reproduced in the printed paper and is not reproduced here.]*

| Field name | Data type |

- **CarCode** (AB1, CD2, M41...) mixes letters and digits, so it is text; it is not used in calculations.
- **CarName** (Toyota Avensis...) is text.
- **UnitPrice** is a quantity that will be multiplied by a number of cars sold, so it must be numeric and not text. The largest price is 3 000 000: this is more than 32 767, the limit of the 16-bit *Integer* type, so the field size must be *Long Integer* (up to 2 147 483 647) or the type *Currency*. A *Single* or *Double* number would also hold the value but is not needed for whole francs.

Marking idea (2 marks): text types for CarCode and CarName (1); a numeric type for UnitPrice (1).

questions.enonce_markdown:
State the possible keys of the database.

Primary key(s) ........ *[2 marks]*

Foreign key(s) ........ *[1 mark]*

State the composite keys if any ........ *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
The three tables are **Cars** (CarCode, CarName, UnitPrice), **Broker** (BrokerID, BrokerName and the other details of the broker) and **Sales** (the transaction: date, BrokerID, CarCode, quantity). The fields of Broker and Sales come from the workbook supplied on the day; the key fields BrokerID and CarCode are the ones used by the questions of Task B.

**Primary keys (2 marks).**
- **Cars**: `CarCode` (each car code is different and never empty).
- **Broker**: `BrokerID` (C001, C002, ... C010: one value per broker).
- **Sales**: no single field is different for every transaction (a broker sells many times and the same car is sold many times), so Sales has no simple primary key; it has a composite key (below).

**Foreign keys (1 mark).** In **Sales**: `BrokerID` (it refers to Broker.BrokerID) and `CarCode` (it refers to Cars.CarCode). A foreign key is a field that is the primary key of another table and that links the two tables.

**Composite key (2 marks).** The **Sales** table is identified by a combination of fields, for example (`SaleDate`, `BrokerID`, `CarCode`): the same broker can sell the same car on several days and several cars on the same day, so only the combination of the three is unique. Here BrokerID and CarCode are at the same time parts of the composite key and foreign keys. (If the transactions have no date, the composite key is (BrokerID, CarCode) when a broker records each car once; the key must be adapted to the Sales sheet really supplied.)

questions.enonce_markdown: By studying the three tables, create the relationship linking the three tables in the database. Draw a labelled diagram of the created relationship in the space below. *[3 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Creating the relationships in Access.** Close all the tables, then *Database Tools* > *Relationships*. In *Show Table* add **Broker**, **Cars** and **Sales** and close the window. Then:

1. Drag `BrokerID` of **Broker** onto `BrokerID` of **Sales**. In *Edit Relationships* tick *Enforce Referential Integrity* and click *Create*: Access draws a one-to-many link (1 at the Broker end, the infinity sign at the Sales end).
2. Drag `CarCode` of **Cars** onto `CarCode` of **Sales**, tick *Enforce Referential Integrity* and click *Create* (one-to-many again).
3. Save the layout (Ctrl+S). The two joined fields must have the same data type (Short Text for both pairs) and the primary keys of question 5 must exist first.

**Labelled diagram (to be drawn in the booklet).**

```
+------------------+  1       N  +------------------+  N       1  +------------------+
| BROKER           |-------------| SALES            |-------------| CARS             |
|------------------|   makes     |------------------|   concerns  |------------------|
| BrokerID (PK)    |             | SaleDate         |             | CarCode (PK)     |
| BrokerName       |             | BrokerID (FK)    |             | CarName          |
| ...              |             | CarCode  (FK)    |             | UnitPrice        |
+------------------+             | Quantity         |             +------------------+
                                 +------------------+
```

Reading: one broker makes many sales (1 - N) and each sale is made by one broker; one car appears in many sales (1 - N) and each sale concerns one car. **Sales** is the table in the middle that links the two others: it turns the many-to-many link between brokers and cars into two one-to-many links.

Marking idea (3 marks): the three tables with their key fields (1); the two links joining the same-named fields (1); the cardinalities 1 and N (infinity) and labels on the links (1).

questions.enonce_markdown:
Use query to produce a summary that will show the cars sold by the various brokers in the various towns on the 13/02/2020 and 14/02/2020. Save the query as **13Sales14**.

**From the database, print the Cars and Sales tables and the 13Sales14 query.** *[4 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Design of the query** (*Create* > *Query Design*). Add the tables **Broker**, **Sales** and **Cars** (the relationships of question 6 supply the joins), then place in the grid:

| Field | Town | BrokerName | CarName | SaleDate | Quantity |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Table | Broker | Broker | Cars | Sales | Sales |
| Total | Group By | Group By | Group By | Where | Sum |
| Criteria | | | | Between #2/13/2020# And #2/14/2020# | |

To get the *Total* row click the *Totals* button (sigma) on the *Design* tab. A *Where* column is not displayed: it only filters the dates, and `Between ... And ...` includes both days, 13/02/2020 and 14/02/2020. (In Access a date criterion is written between # signs in the order month/day/year, for example #2/13/2020#, whatever the regional settings of the computer.) Run the query (*Run*): it lists, for each town and broker, the cars sold and the total quantity (`SumOfQuantity`). Save it with Ctrl+S under the name **13Sales14**.

The same query in SQL (Access syntax, from memory):

```sql
SELECT Broker.Town, Broker.BrokerName, Cars.CarName, Sum(Sales.Quantity) AS TotalSold
FROM (Broker INNER JOIN Sales ON Broker.BrokerID = Sales.BrokerID)
     INNER JOIN Cars ON Cars.CarCode = Sales.CarCode
WHERE Sales.SaleDate Between #2/13/2020# And #2/14/2020#
GROUP BY Broker.Town, Broker.BrokerName, Cars.CarName;
```

Check of the method: the same query with a test range of 14 to 15 February 2020 (ISO dates, run in SQLite on invented data: 3 brokers, 5 cars, 6 sales on 13, 14, 15 and 16 February) kept only the sales of the 14th and 15th, for example Douala / Atabong Colins / Toyota Avensis 1 and Mercedes 220 2, Kumba / Ashu Peter / Toyota Corolla 3, Buea / Beatrice Ngwa / BMW Picnic 1; the sales of the 13th and of the 16th were excluded.

If a plain list of the sales is wanted instead of totals, remove the *Totals* row: each sale is then shown on its own line with its date.

**Printing.** Open **Cars** in *Datasheet View* and use *File* > *Print* (check *Print Preview*); do the same for **Sales** and for the query **13Sales14**; staple the three printouts in the booklet.

Marking idea (4 marks): the right tables and joins (1); the fields Town, BrokerName, CarName and Quantity (1); the date criterion covering the two days (1); query saved under the right name and the three printouts (1).

(The Broker table is assumed to hold the Town of each broker, as the question speaks of brokers in towns; the real field names come from the workbook supplied on the day.)
